sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报《Dealbook》的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的Dealbook峰会上，与商业、政治和文化领域的一些重量级领袖进行现场对话，其中包括J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些坦率、未经修饰的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费阅读我们所有的独家新闻一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The federal government and 48 attorneys general are seeking to break up Facebook, saying that it's become an unlawful monopoly that is hurting consumers.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府和48位总检察长正寻求拆分Facebook，称其已成为损害消费者利益的非法垄断企业。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Mike Isaac takes us inside one of the deals at the center of that claim.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事迈克·艾萨克将带我们深入了解该指控核心的一起交易。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, December 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月17日，星期四。

sentences.en: Mike, where does the story of Facebook and Instagram begin?
sentences.zh: 迈克，Facebook和Instagram的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: I think you have to go back to 2010, which, you know, for us now seems like a bygone era of the internet, basically.
sentences.zh: 我想你得回到2010年，对我们来说，那现在基本上已经像是互联网的过去式了。

sentences.en: But if you can remember, this was back when we were all using Facebook, you know, on our desktop computers.
sentences.zh: 但如果你还记得的话，那是我们所有人都在台式电脑上使用Facebook的时候。

sentences.en: It was more a relic of I sit down and look in my desktop, maybe not even a laptop, and I post photos or status updates to my Facebook there.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一种古董——我坐在桌前看着台式机，甚至可能还不是笔记本电脑，然后把照片或状态更新发布到Facebook上。

sentences.en: So, very different era, very different Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个完全不同的时代，一个完全不同的Facebook。

sentences.en: For 2010, we're going to take the biggest leap since the original iPhone.
sentences.zh: 对于2010年，我们将迎来原版iPhone以来最大的一次飞跃。

sentences.en: Along that time, this is when really the rise of the smartphone started becoming a thing for people.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时期，智能手机真正开始在人们的生活中兴起。

sentences.en: We're introducing iPhone 4.
sentences.zh: 我们正在推出iPhone 4。

sentences.en: This is really hot.
sentences.zh: 这真的太火了。

sentences.en: It was just sort of a real inflection moment on how people use their computers, and rather than sitting down in front of a desk, it was in our pockets, basically.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是人们使用电脑方式的一个真正转折点，比起坐在办公桌前，它基本上走进了我们的口袋。

sentences.en: So, around this time, two Stanford undergrads, Mike Krieger and Kevin Systrom, decided to start a company together.
sentences.zh: 所以，大约在这个时候，两位斯坦福大学的本科生迈克·克里格和凯文·斯特罗姆决定一起创业。

sentences.en: At the time, it was called Bourbon, after Kevin's love of brown alcoholic liquids, I think.
sentences.zh: 当时，它叫Bourbon，我想是因为凯文喜欢棕色的含酒精液体。

sentences.en: And it was basically a social check-in app.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一个社交签到应用。

sentences.en: You say, hi, this is where I am.
sentences.zh: 你说，嗨，这就是我在的地方。

sentences.en: I'm at the store or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我在商店或者其他什么地方。

sentences.en: And then almost immediately, you know, it doesn't catch on.
sentences.zh: 然后几乎立刻，你知道，它并没有流行起来。

sentences.en: Competitors like Foursquare seem to be doing much better.
sentences.zh: 像Foursquare这样的竞争对手似乎做得好得多。

sentences.en: So, they're trying to figure out what to do, what the next steps are.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们一直在想该怎么做，下一步该迈向何方。

sentences.en: And they essentially notice everyone really likes the ability to post photos, to attach a photo to their check-ins.
sentences.zh: 然后他们基本上注意到，大家都非常喜欢发布照片的功能，喜欢在签到时附上一张照片。

sentences.en: And, you know, suddenly, you know, Kevin gets this bright idea.
sentences.zh: 而且，你懂的，突然之间，凯文想出了这个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: It's like, what if we, instead of focusing on the check-in, we focus on letting people post photos from their phones?
sentences.zh: 就像是，如果我们不专注于签到，而是专注于让人们从手机上发布照片，会怎么样？

sentences.en: They do a hard pivot, and Bourbon becomes what we now know as Instagram.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了彻底的转型，Bourbon成为了我们现在所知的Instagram。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how many of you have heard of Instagram, but I love it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你们有多少人听说过Instagram，但我太爱它了。

sentences.en: Instagram allows users to take photos with a vintage look and instantly share them.
sentences.zh: Instagram允许用户拍摄带有复古风格的照片并即时分享。

sentences.en: The real thing that resonated with folks is the filter.
sentences.zh: 真正引起人们共鸣的是滤镜。

sentences.en: It makes your photos better.
sentences.zh: 它能让你的照片更好看。

sentences.en: These filters make your photos better.
sentences.zh: 这些滤镜能让你的照片更出色。

sentences.en: With a free app that allows you to take any picture and make it a memory.
sentences.zh: 通过一个免费的应用程序，你可以拍下任何照片并将其变成回忆。

sentences.en: So, it looks like an old black and white, or even a Polaroid.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来像一张老旧的黑白照片，甚至像宝丽来照片。

sentences.en: Any dude on the street can take a photo and suddenly become Ansel Adams after you sort of tweak the visuals a little bit.
sentences.zh: 任何街头小卒拍张照片，只要稍微调整一下视觉效果，突然之间就能变成安塞尔·亚当斯。

sentences.en: Right, the black and white filter, man.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是那个黑白滤镜，老兄。

sentences.en: Everybody was capable of epic photography.
sentences.zh: 每个人都能拍出史诗级的摄影作品。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was blowing up in 2011.
sentences.zh: 它在2011年彻底火了。

sentences.en: At the time, I remember going to Silicon Valley little startup parties and mixers, and it was the thing everyone was showing to each other on their phones.
sentences.zh: 当时，我记得去硅谷参加一些小型初创公司的派对和聚会，那是每个人都在手机上向其他人展示的东西。

sentences.en: This was kind of how app discovery happened, when it was just like, oh, what are you using?
sentences.zh: 这就是发现应用的方式，当时就是，哦，你在用什么？

sentences.en: Oh, this is what I got.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是我用的。

sentences.en: And it was always Instagram.
sentences.zh: 而每次都是Instagram。

sentences.en: Everyone with an iPhone had Instagram, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上每个拥有iPhone的人都在用Instagram。

sentences.en: So, Mike, as this is happening, what does Facebook, at this point, the biggest social networking company in the United States, what does it make of Instagram?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，当这一切发生时，当时的美国最大社交网络公司Facebook对Instagram怎么看？

sentences.en: Because, as you said, posting photos, sharing photos, that's happening on Facebook, but probably not at the same level as it's happening on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，发照片、分享照片，这在Facebook上也有发生，但可能没有Instagram上那么普及。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, down in Silicon Valley, Mark Zuckerberg, Facebook's founder and CEO, is just watching Instagram blow up.
sentences.zh: 对，所以在硅谷，Facebook创始人兼CEO马克·扎克伯格正看着Instagram一路爆红。

sentences.en: I think he's always kept an eye on competition, but he's had a real eye for what the next big thing is and how people share things.
sentences.zh: 我想他一直都在密切关注竞争对手，但他对下一个重大趋势以及人们如何分享事物有着敏锐的洞察力。

sentences.en: And I think almost immediately, he saw how quickly, how popular posting photos to Instagram was and sort of intuitively knew this is the direction that people are going.
sentences.zh: 我想几乎立刻，他就看到了在Instagram上发照片的速度有多快、人气有多高，并且凭直觉意识到这就是人们未来的发展方向。

sentences.en: Everyone has a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有智能手机。

sentences.en: Everyone's taking photos all the time.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在不停地拍照。

sentences.en: Everyone needs a place to put them.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要一个地方来存放它们。

sentences.en: I want it to be Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我希望这个地方是Facebook。

sentences.en: And so, Zuckerberg and Facebook basically have to decide, do we build something comparable to Instagram or do we just buy them outright?
sentences.zh: 因此，扎克伯格和Facebook基本上必须做出决定：是我们自己开发一个堪比Instagram的产品，还是直接把它买下来？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I actually have some emails right here that Zuckerberg was sending to his lieutenants at the time when they're grappling with this internally.
sentences.zh: 我这里正好有一些扎克伯格当时在内部纠结时发给他手下高管的电子邮件。

sentences.en: And let me read a few.
sentences.zh: 让我读几封。

sentences.en: In one email discussing Instagram, Zuckerberg said, quote,
sentences.zh: 在其中一封讨论Instagram的邮件中，扎克伯格说，引述如下：

sentences.en: The businesses are nascent, but if they grow to a large scale, they could be very disruptive to us.
sentences.zh: 这些业务虽然还处于萌芽期，但如果它们发展到一定规模，可能会对我们造成极大的颠覆。

sentences.en: And in another email, he said, quote,
sentences.zh: 而在另一封邮件中，他说，引述如下：

sentences.en: Instagram can hurt us meaningfully without becoming a huge business.
sentences.zh: Instagram无需成长为庞大业务，就能对我们造成实质性的伤害。

sentences.en: And so, Mark Zuckerberg decides to pull the trigger.
sentences.zh: 于是，马克·扎克伯格决定采取行动。

sentences.en: Well, this just in, a big announcement from Facebook.
sentences.zh: 好了，刚刚收到消息，Facebook发布了一项重大公告。

sentences.en: While one picture might be worth a thousand words, it seems that a whole network of pictures is worth about one billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 俗话说一图胜千言，但现在看来，一整张照片网络价值大约十亿美元。

sentences.en: And Facebook buys Instagram for a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: Facebook以十亿美元收购了Instagram。

sentences.en: A company with only 13 employees bought today by Facebook for one billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 一家只有13名员工的公司今天被Facebook以十亿美元收购。

sentences.en: A billion dollars of money for a thing that kind of ruins your pictures.
sentences.zh: 花十亿美元买一个某种程度上会毁掉你照片的东西。

sentences.en: His company doesn't even make money.
sentences.zh: 这家公司甚至都不赚钱。

sentences.en: But as of today, it's worth more than the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 但截至今天，它的价值已经超过了《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: So rather than building its own version of Instagram that would compete with Instagram, Facebook just buys it out.
sentences.zh: 因此，Facebook没有去打造一个与Instagram竞争的自研版本，而是直接将其买下。

sentences.en: Yep, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: To a lot of people, I think that was really crazy at the time because no one had ever paid that much money to acquire what was essentially a smartphone app.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，我当时觉得这真的很疯狂，因为从来没有人花过那么多钱去收购一个本质上只是智能手机应用的东西。

sentences.en: And everyone just suddenly became newly minted paper millionaires overnight, including Kevin and Mikey, the two founders.
sentences.zh: 而且每个人在一夜之间都成了身家纸面百万富翁，包括两位创始人凯文和迈基。

sentences.en: And what about regulators, Mike?
sentences.zh: 那监管机构呢，迈克？

sentences.en: Do they raise any questions about this deal?
sentences.zh: 他们对这笔交易提出什么疑问了吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: Not at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时没有。

sentences.en: The Federal Trade Commission, which is the government agency that reviews these kind of mergers and acquisitions, you know,
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会，也就是负责审查这类兼并和收购的政府机构，你知道的，

sentences.en: started their usual review process looking into the deal.
sentences.zh: 开始了他们例行的审查流程来调查这笔交易。

sentences.en: Whether they believed it was immediately anti-competitive, whether it was Facebook just sort of pouncing to kill off a competitor that consolidates the market.
sentences.zh: 无论是评估它是否具有即时的反竞争性，还是认为Facebook只是在猛扑过去扼杀一个巩固市场的竞争对手。

sentences.en: But I think it was a different time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为当时是一个不同的时期。

sentences.en: I think at this point there were really questions swirling around whether Facebook would still exist in a couple of years, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为在那个时候，外界确实存在各种疑虑，比如Facebook是否还能存在几年，你知道的，

sentences.en: or whether it would go the way of Friendster or MySpace or once popular social networks like those that people can barely remember them if they weren't, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者它是否会步Friendster、MySpace或那些曾经流行、如果不是当时在用的话几乎会被人遗忘的社交网络的后尘。

sentences.en: using them at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当时人们并没有敲响即时的警报。

sentences.en: So I just don't think immediate alarm bells were going off for people.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么交易完成后接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so what happens next after the deal is done?
sentences.zh: 一切进展如何？

sentences.en: How does it all go?
sentences.zh: 所以到了2014年，Instagram与其说是硅谷的一项创新，不如说是流行文化的一个产物。

sentences.en: So by 2014, Instagram is less an innovation of Silicon Valley and more just sort of a product of pop culture.
sentences.zh: 到那时它甚至变成了一个动词。

sentences.en: By then it became like a verb.
sentences.zh: 我要Instagram一下我的拿铁，或者我要Instagram那个等等。

sentences.en: I'm going to Instagram my latte or I'm going to Instagram that or whatever.
sentences.zh: 等等，不好意思。

sentences.en: Wait, excuse me.
sentences.zh: 我想那个词应该是gram it。

sentences.en: I think the phrase is gram it.
sentences.zh: 不过好吧。

sentences.en: But okay.
sentences.zh: 我暴露年龄了。

sentences.en: I'm showing my age.
sentences.zh: 它开始出现在嘻哈歌词中。

sentences.en: It starts showing up in hip-hop lyrics.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，艺术家和流行文化名人，从她的Instagram来看，金·卡戴珊对她五岁的侄子着迷不已。

sentences.en: You know, artists and pop culture celebrities, judging by her Instagram, Kim Kardashian is obsessed with her five-year-old nephew.
sentences.zh: 首先，泰勒·斯威夫特在Instagram上发布了她和表亲们的这张照片。

sentences.en: First up, Taylor Swift posting this photo of her and her cousins on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 开始使用Instagram并更多地展示他们的生活。

sentences.en: Are starting to get on Instagram and show their lives more.
sentences.zh: 它真的，它成了一股力量。

sentences.en: It's really, it becomes a force.
sentences.zh: 我认为照片分享以及用Instagram捕捉到的这种亲密感，几乎立刻让每个人都清楚，这是社交网络的下一波浪潮。

sentences.en: And I think photo sharing and this sort of intimacy that you can capture with Instagram is almost immediately clear to everyone that this is the next wave of social networking.
sentences.zh: 是的，说实话，我永远不会忘记我意识到那一刻：如果我关注奥普拉·温弗瑞，

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm going to be honest and say I'll never forget the moment I realized that if I followed Oprah Winfrey,
sentences.zh: 我就能进入她私人飞机的内部，她和她的狗在一间带有床的客舱里睡觉。

sentences.en: I was going to have access to the interior of her private plane where she and her dog sleep in a cabin with a bed.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪，我得关注她。

sentences.en: Oh my God, I need to follow her.
sentences.zh: 我之前不知道这个。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，马克·扎克伯格的雷达再次转动，因为他注意到另一个应用在应用商店里迅速崛起。

sentences.en: So it was around this time that Mark Zuckerberg's antenna pop up again because he noticed another app creeping up in the app store very quickly.
sentences.zh: 托尼，Snapchat上每天发送的图片高达3.5亿张。

sentences.en: 350 million images are sent on Snapchat every single day, Tony.
sentences.zh: 哇，哇，哇，哇。

sentences.en: Wow, wow, wow, wow.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 那个应用就是Snapchat。

sentences.en: And that app was Snapchat.
sentences.zh: Snapchat的核心杀手锏在于，你可以拍照，而这些照片在24小时后就会消失。

sentences.en: The killer feature in Snapchat was the idea that you could take photos and they would go away after 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 这个深受人们喜爱的产品被称为“快拍”（Stories）。

sentences.en: This product that people really liked called Stories.
sentences.zh: 扎克伯格立刻看到了人们对此的热烈反应。

sentences.en: And Zuckerberg immediately saw how people were responding to it.
sentences.zh: 所以就像对Instagram一样，他决定Facebook必须对此采取行动。

sentences.en: So just like Instagram, he decided Facebook had to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 于是他最终抛出橄榄枝，出资30亿美元收购Snapchat。

sentences.en: So he ended up making an overture and offering $3 billion to buy Snapchat.
sentences.zh: 但与Instagram不同的是，Snapchat的创始人基本上拒绝了他，并表示，不，我们要走自己的路，建立自己的网络。

sentences.en: But unlike Instagram, Snapchat's founders rebuff him basically and say, no, I think we're going to do our own thing and build our own network.
sentences.zh: 所以扎克伯格决定，好吧，既然你不加入我，那你就是与我为敌，于是开始在内部讨论如何应对Snapchat带来的问题。

sentences.en: So Zuckerberg decides, OK, well, if you're not going to join me, then you're against me and starts internally discussing how they're going to deal with the Snapchat problem.
sentences.zh: 这最终促使他们选定Instagram作为对抗Snapchat的秘密武器。

sentences.en: And that eventually leads to settling on Instagram as their secret weapon to go up against Snapchat.
sentences.zh: Instagram推出了一项名为“快拍”的新功能，是的，它看起来和Snapchat非常像。

sentences.en: Instagram has a new feature called Stories, and yes, it looks a lot like Snapchat.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太耳熟了。

sentences.en: That sounds so familiar.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这灵感是从哪来的。

sentences.en: I wonder where that came from.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个Snapchat的功能。

sentences.en: It's certainly a Snapchat feature.
sentences.zh: 因此，凯文、迈基和扎克伯格创造了本质上是Snapchat“快拍”的克隆版，名字自然就叫Instagram“快拍”。

sentences.en: So Kevin, Mikey, and Zuckerberg create what essentially is a clone of Snapchat Stories, and it's called, naturally, Instagram Stories.
sentences.zh: 所以根本不掩饰这里在发生什么。

sentences.en: So not hiding what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 快拍，那基本上就是对Snapchat快拍的公开抄袭。

sentences.en: Stories, that was basically a blatant copying of Snapchat Stories.
sentences.zh: 而且它成功了。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 所有在Snapchat上发布快拍的人突然发现他们也可以在Instagram上这样做，而且，你知道的，它几乎立刻扼杀了Snapchat的增长势头。

sentences.en: Everyone that was posting stories to Snapchat suddenly finds that they can do it in Instagram, and, you know, it almost immediately kneecaps Snapchat's growth.
sentences.zh: 我不认为Snapchat从那个时刻起完全恢复过元气。

sentences.en: And I don't think Snapchat ever fully recovered from that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克，此时此刻，为了总结我们所讨论的内容：Facebook看到了Instagram的威胁并买下了它，消除了威胁；

sentences.en: So, Mike, at this point, just to summarize the ground we've covered, Facebook sees a threat in Instagram and buys it, neutralizes that threat,
sentences.zh: 看到了Snapchat的威胁但买不下来，于是正如你所说，利用Instagram去扼杀Snapchat。

sentences.en: sees a threat in Snapchat but can't buy it, so uses Instagram to, as you said, kneecap Snapchat.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，扎克伯格似乎已经非常擅长通过收购或搞垮竞争对手来解决问题了。

sentences.en: So by this point, Zuckerberg seems to have gotten very good at either buying or disabling his competitors.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 但到了2018年底，发生了一件令人震惊的事情，我想谁也没有真正预料到。

sentences.en: But by the end of 2018, something shocking happens that I don't think anyone really saw coming.
sentences.zh: Instagram的创始人决定离开Facebook。

sentences.en: The Instagram founders decide that they're going to leave Facebook.
sentences.zh: 他们为什么决定离开？

sentences.en: And why did they decide to leave?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，扎克伯格最初向他们承诺完全的自主权。

sentences.en: So, you know, Zuckerberg initially promised them this full autonomy.
sentences.zh: 但到了2018年，他开始做一些微调和改变，基本上试图把Instagram和Facebook拉得更近一些，将它们融合在一起，

sentences.en: But by 2018, he starts to make these little tweaks and changes that essentially try to push Instagram and Facebook together a little bit more, meld them together,
sentences.zh: 把它们变成Instagram创始人并不希望看到的样子。

sentences.en: and make them into something that the Instagram founders didn't want.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们想要自己的自主权。

sentences.en: You know, they wanted their autonomy.
sentences.zh: 他们希望在没有Facebook的干涉或内部纽带的情况下打造这个产品。

sentences.en: They wanted to sort of build this product without Facebook's hooks inside of it or connective tissue there.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这不是我们当初加入时的协议。

sentences.en: They said, that's not what we signed up for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们当初签署协议时的初衷。

sentences.en: We don't like the direction this is going.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢事情这样发展下去。

sentences.en: Here's our resignation.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的辞呈。

sentences.en: See you later.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: So I think their resignations come, you know, at a time where folks are starting to question a lot of fundamental things about Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得他们的辞职，你知道，发生在一个人们开始对脸书的许多根本问题产生质疑的时期。

sentences.en: St. Petersburg's notorious troll factory is finally giving up its secrets.
sentences.zh: 圣彼得堡声名狼藉的水军工厂终于要公开它的秘密了。

sentences.en: You know, whether the company's good for democracy at large.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是这家公司对整个民主体制到底有没有好处。

sentences.en: Reports in the New York Times and Britain's Observer suggest Facebook data was misused to sway voters in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》和英国《观察家报》的报道表明，脸书的数据被滥用于左右2016年大选的选民。

sentences.en: You know, they don't care about your privacy, your right to not share everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们根本不在乎你的隐私，不在乎你拥有不分享一切的权利。

sentences.en: Cambridge Analytica misused the data of 50 million Americans collected from Facebook.
sentences.zh: 剑桥分析公司滥用了从脸书收集的50多万名美国人的数据。

sentences.en: Mark Zuckerberg found himself at the heart of America's democracy, delivering an apology.
sentences.zh: 马克·扎克伯格发现自己处在美国民主的风口浪尖，并作出了道歉。

sentences.en: That was a big mistake.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: And it was my mistake.
sentences.zh: 而且那是我的错。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 对此我深表歉意。

sentences.en: The bloom was off the rose officially.
sentences.zh: 好景不长，昔日的辉煌正式烟消云散了。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此，完全如此。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，甚至不需要绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Mike, tell me about this major lawsuit that was filed last week and how it is that Instagram fits into it.
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，跟我讲讲上周起诉的那起重大诉讼，以及Instagram是如何卷入其中的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the FTC and, you know, attorney generals across almost all 50 U.S.
sentences.zh: 好的，联邦贸易委员会，还有，你知道的，几乎全美50个州的司法部长

sentences.en: states basically come out swinging against Facebook.
sentences.zh: 基本上都开始对脸书发起猛烈抨击。

sentences.en: And these pair of really large, really sort of far-reaching lawsuits against the company would say that over the past 10 years, basically,
sentences.zh: 这两起规模宏大、影响深远的针对该公司的诉讼表明，在过去10年里，基本上，

sentences.en: Facebook has attempted to create a monopoly on social media for consumers in the United States.
sentences.zh: 脸书一直试图在美国消费者的社交媒体市场上制造垄断。

sentences.en: And specifically in the company's history of acquisitions and in Mark Zuckerberg's pursuing companies like Instagram,
sentences.zh: 特别是在该公司收购的历史上，以及马克·扎克伯格追求像Instagram这样的公司时，

sentences.en: companies like WhatsApp, making these billion-dollar acquisitions, he did it with the intent to kill off any sort of competition he might have in the marketplace
sentences.zh: 像WhatsApp这样的公司，进行这些数十亿美元的收购时，他这样做的目的就是为了扼杀他在市场可能面临的任何竞争

sentences.en: and to essentially become the one true social network.
sentences.zh: 并从本质上成为唯一真正的社交网络。

sentences.en: The even further-reaching argument is that, you know, the FTC and the AGs want to essentially cut up Facebook into a bunch of different parts.
sentences.zh: 更深远的论点是，联邦贸易委员会和各州司法部长基本上想把脸书拆分成许多不同的部分。

sentences.en: We know, spin off Instagram, spin off WhatsApp, spin off some of the most important parts of Facebook's business and future growth in the long term.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，剥离Instagram，剥离WhatsApp，剥离脸书业务和未来长期增长中最重要的一些部分。

sentences.en: And what they said is that that will essentially help consumers have more choice in social media in the marketplace
sentences.zh: 他们表示，从本质上讲，这将有助于消费者在市场上的社交媒体方面有更多选择

sentences.en: and protect them from Facebook sort of controlling all the social media landscape, controlling what privacy choices are, controlling how much data you share,
sentences.zh: 并保护他们免受脸书对所有社交媒体格局的控制、对隐私选择的控制、对你分享多少数据的控制，

sentences.en: controlling one company from having a view over everything we do on social media.
sentences.zh: 控制一家公司对我们在社交媒体上所做的一切的掌控。

sentences.en: I think it's worth pausing and just observing what an enormous deal this lawsuit is.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有必要停下来，观察一下这场诉讼是多么重大的一件事。

sentences.en: I mean, it is a very rare thing in the United States, in this free market economy,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在美国，在这个自由市场经济中，这非常罕见，

sentences.en: for our government to file a legal action that attempts to break up a major company that's in all of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们的政府采取法律行动，试图拆分一家融入我们所有人生活的龙头企业。

sentences.en: I mean, the last time this happened, I was a kid, you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，上一次发生这种事时，我还是个孩子，你也是个孩子。

sentences.en: It was when the United States government did this to Microsoft, and that was historic.
sentences.zh: 那是美国政府对微软采取行动的时候，那具有历史意义。

sentences.en: It was the biggest business story of its time, and it hasn't really happened since.
sentences.zh: 那是当时最大的商业新闻，此后再也没有真正发生过。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think this is really, you know, one of the biggest cases, probably the biggest case to happen in Silicon Valley in ages.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这真的是，你知道的，最大的案件之一，可能是硅谷很久以来发生的最大案件。

sentences.en: You know, it's been 20 years since the landmark Microsoft case, and we haven't seen anything since as far-reaching and as aggressive by the government since this Facebook lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，距离具有里程碑意义的微软案已经过去20年了，自这次脸书诉讼以来，我们再也没有见过政府如此深远且咄咄逼人的举动了。

sentences.en: And how central is the Instagram deal that we spent so much time just talking about to the government's case?
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚花了那么多时间讨论的Instagram交易，对政府的案件来说有多核心？

sentences.en: It feels pretty central.
sentences.zh: 感觉相当核心。

sentences.en: I think it's really key.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很关键。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we can look back over the evidence that they've presented in their lawsuit so far,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我们可以回顾一下他们在诉讼中迄今为止提出的证据，

sentences.en: and a lot of the, you know, most questionable quotes from Zuckerberg revolve around his decision to buy Instagram in particular early on.
sentences.zh: 而且许多，你知道的，扎克伯格最受质疑的言论，都围绕着他早期决定收购Instagram这一举动。

sentences.en: His questions around, do we need to worry about them?
sentences.zh: 他提出的那些问题，比如我们需要担心他们吗？

sentences.en: Is this something we have to do?
sentences.zh: 这是我们必须做的事吗？

sentences.en: Is this, are they going to be a viable threat at some point?
sentences.zh: 这是，他们会在某个时候成为一个现实的威胁吗？

sentences.en: You know, versions of those types of questions that he's batting around internally.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是他在内部反复权衡的那些问题的各种版本。

sentences.en: So what was once the ideal of a tech acquisition is now becoming this sort of Achilles heel for Facebook,
sentences.zh: 所以曾经作为科技收购理想的案例，现在正成为脸书的阿喀琉斯之踵，

sentences.en: and the types of questions that were being asked internally are now being revisited by regulators in a way that didn't really happen at the time.
sentences.zh: 当年在内部提出的那些问题，现在正被监管机构重新审视，这是当时并未真正发生的情况。

sentences.en: So those emails that Zuckerberg sent that you had read to us from 2011, 2012, saying, wow, Instagram, we should be worried, we should do something about that.
sentences.zh: 所以扎克伯格在2011年、2012年发给你的那些被你读给我们听的电子邮件，上面写着，哇，Instagram，我们应该担心，我们应该采取点行动。

sentences.en: Those are now being presented as evidence of kind of anti-competitive monopolistic behavior of a company trying to basically snuff out its competitors.
sentences.zh: 这些现在都被作为证据，证明一家公司试图扼杀其竞争对手的反竞争垄断行为。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think, you know, they're looking back on 15 years of emails, basically, and trying to sort of say Facebook, in its ascent to being a network used by 3 billion people,
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，他们基本上是在回顾15年的电子邮件，并试图说明脸书在成长为一个拥有30亿用户网络的过程中，

sentences.en: most of the United States has along the way crushed any idea of competition in the U.S., and that's not legal.
sentences.zh: 美国的大多数人在这个过程中粉碎了美国任何竞争的想法，这是不合法的。

sentences.en: And what does Facebook say in response to this?
sentences.zh: 对此脸书作何回应？

sentences.en: I'm guessing they see this all very differently, especially when it comes to an acquisition like Instagram.
sentences.zh: 我猜他们对此有非常不同的看法，特别是在涉及像Instagram这样的收购时。

sentences.en: Oh, man, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，是的。

sentences.en: They're not taking it lying down.
sentences.zh: 他们不会逆来顺受的。

sentences.en: I mean, to be clear, this is existential for Facebook, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，明确地说，这对脸书来说是生死攸关的，对吧？

sentences.en: The government wants to break off one of the most high-growth apps that Facebook owns, Instagram, this thing that young people like.
sentences.zh: 政府想要剥离脸书旗下增长最快的应用之一——Instagram，这个深受年轻人喜爱的产品。

sentences.en: They still see skyrocketing usage all over the world.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然看到该应用在全世界范围内使用量呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: This is really key.
sentences.zh: 这真的很关键。

sentences.en: So they've laid out, you know, some pretty compelling points in return to the government's argument.
sentences.zh: 所以他们针对政府的论点，也提出了一些非常令人信服的观点。

sentences.en: Basically, for one, the FTC did not challenge the acquisition eight years ago when it happened.
sentences.zh: 基本上，首先，八年前联邦贸易委员会收购发生时并未提出异议。

sentences.en: And so they're basically saying you essentially want a do-over.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是在说，你们本质上是想重新来过。

sentences.en: I think another thing, too, was Instagram wasn't huge at the time that Facebook bought them.
sentences.zh: 我想还有一点，那就是脸书收购Instagram时，它并不是很大。

sentences.en: And that, you know, potentially, if Facebook had not bought Instagram, it wouldn't necessarily be the behemoth it was today.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果脸书没有收购Instagram，它可能不一定会成为今天的庞然大物。

sentences.en: You know, we have no real way of knowing that either way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论如何我们都没有真正的办法知道这一点。

sentences.en: That's just an alternate version of history.
sentences.zh: 那只是历史的另一种版本。

sentences.en: But that's what Facebook's argument is.
sentences.zh: 但这就是脸书的论点。

sentences.en: We helped it become as big as it is.
sentences.zh: 我们帮助它长得这么大。

sentences.en: Third, you know, it's free.
sentences.zh: 第三，你知道，它是免费的。

sentences.en: People don't have to pay for any of Facebook's services.
sentences.zh: 人们不必为脸书的任何服务付费。

sentences.en: So it's not like, you know, Facebook bought Instagram and suddenly jacked up the price and now consumers are getting harmed.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像，你知道，脸书收购了Instagram然后突然抬高价格，导致消费者受到伤害。

sentences.en: And so, you know, if you feel like you don't want to use it anymore, then just go take your stuff elsewhere, basically, is what they say.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你觉得你不想再用了，那就把你的东西拿到别处去，基本上，这就是他们的说法。

sentences.en: And then, you know, finally, there have been other competitors that have popped up in the interim, right?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，最后，在此期间还出现了其他竞争对手，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, TikTok has grown immensely in just the past two or three years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，TikTok在过去两三年里增长巨大。

sentences.en: You know, Parler, even this new social media company for conservatives, that has been growing, growing a lot in the past few months.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Parler，甚至这个面向保守派的新社交媒体公司，在过去几个月里一直在增长，增长了很多。

sentences.en: I think Facebook even sees iMessage on iPhones as a threat.
sentences.zh: 我想脸书甚至将iPhone上的iMessage视为一种威胁。

sentences.en: So really, the definition of how many social networks are out there that compete with Facebook, they feel like is much bigger than the FTC and the AGs are recognizing.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，与脸书竞争的社交网络数量的定义，他们觉得比联邦贸易委员会和各州司法部长所认识到的要广泛得多。

sentences.en: So, Mike, given those arguments, how strong is the legal case being brought against Facebook?
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克，鉴于这些论点，针对脸书的法律诉讼有多大胜算？

sentences.en: I'm sure you talk to lots of people about it.
sentences.zh: 我确信你和很多人谈过这件事。

sentences.en: Is it considered a strong case?
sentences.zh: 这被认为是一个强有力的案件吗？

sentences.en: Is it considered a weak case?
sentences.zh: 这被认为是一个软弱的案件吗？

sentences.en: Even this has contention among legal scholars.
sentences.zh: 甚至在法律学者中也存在这种争议。

sentences.en: There are folks like Tim Wu, who's a professor who's followed this antitrust stuff for a long time, who believes all they have to do, all the government has to do,
sentences.zh: 有一些人，比如蒂姆·吴，他是一位长期关注反垄断问题的教授，他认为他们所需要做的，政府所需要做的，

sentences.en: is prove that Facebook has a history of trying to snuff out the competition systematically over time.
sentences.zh: 就是证明脸书有着随着时间推移系统性试图扼杀竞争的历史。

sentences.en: And you can point to the emails in Facebook's own history and just sort of make the case that way.
sentences.zh: 你可以指出脸书自身历史上的电子邮件，然后以这种方式阐明案件。

sentences.en: I think there are other folks who think that the government has a tough case.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有其他人认为政府面临着一个艰难的案件。

sentences.en: I think that you have to sort of, the way antitrust law is written, prove that you're doing harm to consumers.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须，按照反垄断法的编写方式，证明你对消费者造成了损害。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are probably not as many clear-cut cases of, this harms me directly because people can kind of come and go as they please.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，可能没有那么多明确的案例，这直接伤害了我，因为人们可以随心所欲地来去自由。

sentences.en: What the government will say is, you know, one company owning everything can erode users' choices around privacy over time.
sentences.zh: 政府会说，你知道，一家公司拥有一切会随着时间推移侵蚀用户对隐私的选择。

sentences.en: And so, if you want to talk about consumer harm, if we're stuck in Facebook, Instagram, and other apps that are owned by Facebook,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想谈论消费者损害，如果我们被困在脸书、Instagram和脸书拥有的其他应用中，

sentences.en: we don't have a choice on how much data and information we're sharing about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们就没有选择权来决定我们分享了多少关于我们自己的数据和信息。

sentences.en: And that's the direct part of consumer harm.
sentences.zh: 这就是消费者损害的直接部分。

sentences.en: So, I don't think it's an open-and-shut case for either side.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为对任何一方来说，这都不是一个板上钉钉的案件。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be complicated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是复杂的。

sentences.en: And I also think it's going to take years to figure out.
sentences.zh: 我也认为这需要多年时间才能弄清楚。

sentences.en: Mike, it feels like the case being made against Facebook, at the end of the day, it raises really interesting questions about what exactly it means to be anti-competitive,
sentences.zh: 迈克，感觉针对脸书的案件，归根结底，提出了非常有趣的问题，即反竞争到底意味着什么，

sentences.en: especially in the kind of new world of social media and the digital economy.
sentences.zh: 特别是在社交媒体和数字经济这种新世界中。

sentences.en: Because we have been living in a world of corporate acquisitions for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 因为我们生活在一个企业并购的世界里已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: Businesses buy other businesses.
sentences.zh: 企业收购其他企业。

sentences.en: Airlines buy airlines.
sentences.zh: 航空公司收购航空公司。

sentences.en: Newspapers buy newspapers.
sentences.zh: 报社收购报社。

sentences.en: And startups buy startups.
sentences.zh: 初创公司收购初创公司。

sentences.en: And for the most part, regulators don't get all that involved in stopping these acquisitions.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，监管机构并没有真正参与阻止这些收购。

sentences.en: I mean, the default mode is, congratulations, do your merger.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，默认模式是，恭喜，去做你的合并吧。

sentences.en: So, I wonder why we think the government is so focused on Facebook and on these deals, why it has become the target of this antitrust attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想知道为什么我们认为政府如此专注于脸书和这些交易，为什么它成为了这种反垄断关注的目标。

sentences.en: And is that because of the unusual scale of Facebook, the kind of singular role that Facebook plays in our digital lives?
sentences.zh: 是因为脸书不同寻常的规模，还是脸书在我们数字生活中扮演的那种独特角色？

sentences.en: Is it the fact that Facebook has become the focus of so much controversy, frankly, over the past few years?
sentences.zh: 是因为脸书在过去几年里坦率地成为了如此多争议的焦点吗？

sentences.en: Is it all the above?
sentences.zh: 是以上所有这些吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: I think probably in legal circles and definitely in Washington, there's this perception that, you know, that's in 2010s, right?
sentences.zh: 我想可能在法律界，绝对是在华盛顿，有这样一种看法，你知道，那是2010年代的事了，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, again, like this default mode was sort of anoint each acquisition, let them sail through and not really put up much of a fight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，同样地，这种默认模式有点像是祝福每一次收购，让他们顺利通过，而没有真正进行太多反抗。

sentences.en: I also think that, you know, people looked at tech differently back then and really didn't see the potential harms that some of these networks can do and have on the world.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，你知道，人们当年对技术的看法不同，真的没有看到其中一些网络可以对世界产生并已经产生的潜在危害。

sentences.en: You know, misinformation and using social networks to manipulate democracy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，虚假信息和利用社交媒体操纵民主。

sentences.en: That was not, you know, in my mind when I was taking photos of a latte back in 2010.
sentences.zh: 这可不在我的脑海里，当我2010年拍摄拿铁咖啡的照片时。

sentences.en: That was just, that's a different time, right?
sentences.zh: 那只是，那是不同的时代，对吧？

sentences.en: And so I think, you know, some folks would say it may be years later, but new information has come to light.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，有些人会说这可能是几年后，但新的信息已经大白于天下。

sentences.en: We can understand how these networks work and how they can be harmful to consumers and how having so much power in one particular company can be a bad thing over time.
sentences.zh: 我们可以理解这些网络是如何运作的，它们对消费者有多大危害，以及随着时间的推移，将如此多的权力集中在一家特定公司手中怎么会是一件坏事。

sentences.en: And so now there's political bipartisan support around pursuing companies like Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以现在围绕起诉像脸书这样的公司，存在着两党的政治支持。

sentences.en: Mike, let's imagine for just a moment in a theoretical world that the government, the attorneys general,
sentences.zh: 迈克，让我们在理论世界中想象片刻，如果政府，各州司法部长，

sentences.en: the FTC succeeds in its lawsuit and the courts decide that Facebook should be broken up.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会在诉讼中获胜，法院裁定应该拆分脸书。

sentences.en: How exactly does that work?
sentences.zh: 那到底是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: Because as you said, these businesses, Facebook, Instagram, they've all gotten very interwoven.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，这些企业，脸书，Instagram，它们都已经非常交织在一起了。

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Right now, the executives at Facebook are in the process of integrating the back ends of a few of the apps, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp,
sentences.zh: 目前，脸书的高管们正在整合几个应用的后端，Instagram、Facebook Messenger、WhatsApp，

sentences.en: and basically knitting them all together so that people can message each other across the apps, which is very different than the history of how these apps have been sort of used.
sentences.zh: 并基本上将它们全部编织在一起，以便人们可以在各个应用之间互相发消息，这与这些应用过去的使用历史非常不同。

sentences.en: It's been a years-long project of the past two years, and the question is, by the time this lawsuit gets figured out, if it does order a breakup,
sentences.zh: 这是过去两年里历时多年的项目，问题是，到这起诉讼弄清楚的时候，如果它确实下令拆分，

sentences.en: can you even technically do that at some point?
sentences.zh: 你在技术上甚至能在某些时候做到这一点吗？

sentences.en: Can you disentangle them?
sentences.zh: 你能把它们解开吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Facebook has not said it's going to stop its work on the apps.
sentences.zh: 脸书并没有说它要停止对这些应用的工作。

sentences.en: It's not going to, like, stop knitting them together.
sentences.zh: 它不会像，停止把它们编织在一起。

sentences.en: So I haven't found a good answer from that.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有从中找到一个好的答案。

sentences.en: Definitely not from Facebook, not from technologists quite yet because it's still in process.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是从脸书那里，也不是从技术专家那里，因为这还在进行中。

sentences.en: I still think that if you can put something together, you can probably un-put it together, and Facebook would have to probably find a way to cleave it up.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为，如果你能把某样东西拼凑在一起，你大概就能把它拆开，脸书可能必须找到一种方法把它劈开。

sentences.en: But if Facebook doesn't own Instagram, does that fix the fact that there are, you know, foreign trolls doing damage across the network?
sentences.zh: 但如果脸书不拥有Instagram，这能否解决这样一个事实，即你知道，有外国水军在整个网络中造成破坏？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: Does it change the problem of misinformation, whether it's going to exist or not?
sentences.zh: 这会改变虚假信息的问题吗，无论它是否会存在？

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，它不会。

sentences.en: There's one thing we learned, you know, there's always new problems we're finding out as a result of the internet, and it'll take much longer and, you know,
sentences.zh: 有一件事我们了解到了，你知道，我们总是发现作为互联网结果的新问题，这将需要更长的时间，你知道，

sentences.en: far more different approaches and potential laws and regulations to figure that out rather than, you know, one big action that cleans up everything.
sentences.zh: 需要更多不同的方法以及潜在的法律和法规来解决这个问题，而不是，你知道，采取一个能清理一切的大动作。

sentences.en: Well, Mike, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: This goliath of a company is using its power to manipulate the market, destroy competition, and harm you, the consumer.
sentences.zh: 这家庞大的企业巨头正在利用其力量操纵市场、摧毁竞争，并损害你们这些消费者的利益。

sentences.en: In the latest antitrust case brought against a big tech company, 10 attorneys general accused Google of illegally abusing its power over online advertising.
sentences.zh: 在针对一家大型科技公司提起最新反垄断诉讼中，10位总检察长指控谷歌非法滥用其在网络广告领域的力量。

sentences.en: Let me put it this way.
sentences.zh: 我这样说吧。

sentences.en: If the free market were a baseball game, Google positioned itself as the pitcher, the batter, and the umpire.
sentences.zh: 如果自由市场是一场棒球比赛，谷歌就把自己定位为投手、击球手和裁判。

sentences.en: The lawsuit said that Google now controls software at every step of the ad sales process and has used that power to overcharge clients, a claim that Google denies.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，谷歌现在控制着广告销售流程各个环节的软件，并利用这种权力向客户多收费，谷歌对此予以否认。

sentences.en: And on Wednesday night,
sentences.zh: 而在周三晚上，

sentences.en: congressional leaders said that they were closing in on a roughly $900 billion economic relief package that would include a second round of direct payments to Americans,
sentences.zh: 国会领导人表示，他们即将达成一项约9000亿美元的经济救助计划，其中包括向美国人发放第二轮直接补助、

sentences.en: additional unemployment benefits, and funding for vaccine distribution.
sentences.zh: 额外的失业救济金以及疫苗分发资金。

sentences.en: But the plan omits coronavirus liability protections for companies, which were sought by Republicans, and a dedicated stream of funding for local governments,
sentences.zh: 但该计划没有包含共和党人寻求的对企业的冠状病毒责任保护，也没有包含民主党人寻求的

sentences.en: which was sought by Democrats.
sentences.zh: 针对地方政府的专属资金支持。

sentences.en: A deal could be completed by this morning.
sentences.zh: 一项协议可能会在今天上午达成。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rochelle Banja, Nina Potok, Rachel Quester, and Daniel Guimet, with help from Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由 Rochelle Banja、Nina Potok、Rachel Quester 和 Daniel Guimet 制作，Alexandra Lee Young 提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由 Lisa Chow 编辑，Chris Wood 负责音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时又扣人心弦的权力之争。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》节目中，我和萨拉·凯尼格将带你了解那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: Metro。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
